section_summary.extract_value: This section provides a comprehensive literature review on positive body image constructs, specifically body appreciation and body image flexibility. It discusses how body appreciation transcends simple body satisfaction to include accepting the body with its flaws, being attuned to bodily needs, engaging in self-care, and resisting unrealistic media images. The text reviews empirical evidence showing body appreciation's inverse associations with eating disorders and positive links with psychological well-being, and discusses the emerging construct of body image flexibility rooted in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. The section concludes by noting that the present investigation extends research on body image flexibility in relation to body appreciation and BMI among Black older adolescent females preparing to enter university, addressing a gap in ethnically-diverse samples.
